question: What's new in the latest MATLAB release?
answer:
Based on MATLAB R2026b, released on 23 September 2026 [4], with Update 1 now available as of November 2026 [6].

- **Project and package management:** New TOML-based project files let you manage projects with a single human-readable configuration file, and packages can be shared and installed through File Exchange [5][7]. The blog shows an `mpmuninstall` command for removing packages [4].
- **App Designer and live scripts:** Apps can now be saved in a plain-text format (a combination of .m and .xml files) that works better with source control, though .mlapp is still the default [4][7]. Live scripts now default to the plain-text .m format, with .mlx as the option [4].
- **Performance:** The object performance improvement is installable as a beta add-on, and some operations were reported as over 300x faster [4]. `validatestring` is also faster, with a 5.8x speed-up in the release-note example [4].
- **Java:** MATLAB no longer includes Java, so you install a compatible OpenJDK (including OpenJDK 25) [7].
- **Interoperability and data:** GPU data can be passed between MATLAB and Python without a round trip through host memory [4]. Google Sheets integration was also added [5].
- **Desktop and toolboxes:** The desktop has more flexible layout options [7]. Deep Learning Toolbox adds the Time Series Modeler app and PyTorch co-execution [5]. Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox adds the DOE and Gage R&R apps [7]. Mapping Toolbox adds 3D scenarios [4].
- **New products:** Simulink Variant Manager, Visual Inspection Toolbox, and Polyspace Test Server are new in this release [5].
- **ARM Linux:** MATLAB on Linux ARM (including Raspberry Pi and DGX Spark) is in open beta, built on R2026b Update 1 [6].

The full list is in the official release notes and Release Highlights [4][5].

keyPoints.text: MathWorks released Release 2026b (R2026b) of MATLAB and Simulink on 24 Sep 2026, adding Simulink Variant Manager, Visual Inspection Toolbox, and Polyspace Test Server.
R2026b makes plain-text .m Live Code the default for live scripts, with .mlx becoming the option, and lets App Designer apps be saved as plain text.
MATLAB adds TOML-based project files, package management through File Exchange, and Google Sheets integration in R2026b.
R2026b includes performance gains, including an optional Object Performance Improvement beta and general speed-ups, plus Java no longer being bundled with MATLAB.
A MATLAB on Linux ARM open beta including R2026b Update 1 has been announced for Raspberry Pi and DGX Spark.
